## The surface and the measurement

`pm contracts --summary` is the designated first call of the agent cold start — pm-ka6d exists to document exactly that, and `AGENTS.md` routes agents to it before anything else. Its per-command payload is three fields: the command name, its declared flags, its declared token ceiling, and one line of `intent`. The intent line is the only field that answers *what is this command for*; everything else answers *how do I call it*.

Measured at HEAD on build 2026.8.1: the summary enumerates 76 canonical commands. 32 of them — 42 percent — carry the intent string `"Inspect flags."`, which is the placeholder, not an intent.

```
beads cal calendar changelog close-many close-task command-kit comments-audit
completion-statuses completion-tags completion-types dedupe-audit dedupe-merge
eval event events item meet merge normalize pause-task remind search-advanced
start-task templates test-all test-runs todos twin update-many vcs
```

Package-contributed nouns account for part of that list (`beads`, `todos`, `twin`, `vcs`, `changelog`, `command-kit`, `templates`). The remainder are core: `merge`, `normalize`, `events`, `item`, `update-many`, `eval`, `search-advanced`, `close-many`, `test-all`, `test-runs`, `dedupe-audit`, `dedupe-merge`, `comments-audit`, plus the calendar and lifecycle sugar spellings.

`merge` is the clearest illustration of the cost. It is the entry point to the field-aware branch-merge contract that makes concurrent agents safe, it is the subject of its own documentation chapter, and an agent orienting through the summary is told that its purpose is to inspect flags.

## Why it is a defect rather than missing prose

`summarizeCommandIntent` (`src/sdk/cli-contracts/runtime-contracts.ts:2429`) resolves the exact command, then the root command, then returns `"Inspect flags."`. The fallback is total and silent. It emits no diagnostic, sets no flag on the payload, and produces a well-formed summary row indistinguishable from a described one.

`COMMAND_INTENTS` (`src/sdk/cli-contracts/runtime-contracts.ts:594`) is a hand-maintained `Map`. Nothing joins it against the command catalog. A new command therefore ships with a placeholder intent and every gate stays green, which is why the gap reached 42 percent without anyone noticing: there is no state of the repository in which the omission is visible except by counting.

## What it costs, in the units the surface exists to save

Cold start measured on this workspace: `pm contracts --summary` is 9,701 bytes, roughly 2,425 tokens; `pm next` is 9,912 bytes, roughly 2,478 tokens. The documented two-call orientation is therefore about 4,903 tokens. The full per-command help surface, the thing the summary exists to avoid reading, is 218,872 bytes across 88 command spellings — roughly 54,718 tokens.

The summary buys a 91 percent reduction, and it buys it by promising that one line per command is enough to choose. For 32 commands the line is empty, so the only recovery is `pm <command> --help`, at a median of roughly 580 tokens per command. An agent that needs two of them has spent more than the entire summary cost to recover what the summary was supposed to deliver. That is the exact regression the tiered-help design (pm-e2bq) was built to prevent.

## What this item owns

Intent coverage as a contract rather than a convention. Every command in the catalog resolves to a declared intent; the resolution is total by construction rather than by a fallback string. Package-contributed commands declare their intent through the contribution manifest so an installed package cannot lower the coverage of the surface it extends. Coverage is checked mechanically in the same conformance pass that checks the noun-verb table (pm-wt43zj), so a command without an intent cannot merge.

The intent itself has a shape, because an unconstrained sentence would reintroduce the cost the summary exists to remove: one line, imperative, naming the noun it acts on and the read/write direction, within a declared character budget, and distinct from every other command's intent — two commands with identical intents are as uninformative as two placeholders.

## Boundaries

Not the tiering question (pm-kxci8x): which commands appear in the summary at all is a separate contract from whether the ones that appear are described.

Not the help-text rewrite (pm-e2bq): that owns the rendering tiers and the one-screen core help; this owns the single field the machine-readable summary publishes per command.

Not the token-budget declaration (pm-5t33or): 21 of the same 76 commands declare no `default_max_estimated_tokens`, which is that item's coverage gap on the same payload, found by the same census and worth resolving in the same pass.
The contracts summary answers 'what is this command for' with a silent placeholder for 32 of 76 canonical commands, so the designated agent cold start carries no intent for 42 percent of the surface

summarizeCommandIntent (src/sdk/cli-contracts/runtime-contracts.ts:2429) resolves the exact command, then the root command, then returns the literal 'Inspect flags.' with no diagnostic and no payload marker, and COMMAND_INTENTS (:594) is a hand-maintained Map that nothing joins against the command catalog. Measured at HEAD on 2026.8.1: 32 of 76 canonical commands in pm contracts --summary carry the placeholder, including the core nouns merge, normalize, events, item, update-many, eval, search-advanced, close-many, test-all, test-runs, dedupe-audit, dedupe-merge and comments-audit. The summary is the first call of the documented two-call cold start (pm-ka6d) and costs 2,425 tokens against 54,718 for the full per-command help surface; recovering one missing intent via pm <command> --help costs roughly 580 tokens, so two recoveries exceed the summary's own price. Duplicate check: searched intent/summary/help-tier/one-line lineages and read pm-e2bq, pm-kxci8x, pm-ka6d, pm-wt43zj, pm-5t33or; none owns intent coverage as a contract.

Every command in the catalog resolves to a declared intent by construction with no fallback string; package-contributed commands declare intent through the contribution manifest; intent shape is constrained (imperative, names the noun and read/write direction, within a declared character budget, unique across commands); coverage and uniqueness are machine-checked in the noun-verb conformance pass so a command without an intent cannot merge
Make the machine-readable command summary answer what each command is for, for every command
The 91 percent token saving the summary offers stops being conditional on which command an agent needs
The gap reached 42 percent silently because no state of the repository makes it visible except by counting; each new command widens it
